column1: After a number of serious failures of governance (that is, how they are managed at the highest level), companies in Britain, as well as elsewhere, should consider radical changes to their directors’ roles.
column2: 在接连发生严重的公司治理失误后，也就是在最高管理层的运作上接连出问题后，英国及其他地方的公司都应考虑彻底改变董事的角色。
column5: at the highest level|在最高管理层面

column1: It is clear that the role of a board director today is not an easy one.
column2: 显然，如今当一名公司董事并不轻松。
column5: not an easy one|并非轻松的差事

column1: Following the 2008 financial meltdown, which resulted in a deeper and more prolonged period of economic downturn than anyone expected, the search for explanations in the many post-mortems of the crisis has meant blame has been spread far and wide.
column2: 2008年金融崩溃后，经济低迷比任何人预想的都更严重、持续得更久。人们对危机进行了多番事后剖析，追寻原因的时候，许多方面都受到了指责。

column1: Governments, regulators, central banks and auditors have all been in the frame.
column2: 各国政府、监管机构、中央银行和审计师，都成了被追责的对象。
column7: in the frame|成为被怀疑或追责的对象

column1: The role of bank directors and management and their widely publicised failures have been extensively picked over and examined in reports, inquiries and commentaries.
column2: 各种报告、调查和评论反复细察了银行董事和管理层所起的作用，以及那些已被广泛报道的失误。

column1: The knock-on effect of this scrutiny has been to make the governance of companies in general an issue of intense public debate and has significantly increased the pressures on, and the responsibilities of, directors.
column2: 这种审视带来的连锁反应，是公司治理整体上成为公众激烈争论的问题，董事承受的压力和肩负的责任也大大增加。
column6: intense public debate|激烈的公共争论

column1: At the simplest and most practical level, the time involved in fulfilling the demands of a board directorship has increased significantly, calling into question the effectiveness of the classic model of corporate governance by part-time, independent non-executive directors.
column2: 从最简单、最实际的层面看，履行董事职责所需的时间已经大幅增加。这让人质疑，由兼职的独立非执行董事实施公司治理的经典模式是否有效。
column3: fulfilling the demands|履行职责要求
column9: independent non-executive directors|独立非执行董事

column1: Where once a board schedule may have consisted of between eight and ten meetings a year, in many companies the number of events requiring board input and decisions has dramatically risen.
column2: 过去，董事会一年的日程可能只有八到十次会议；现在，许多公司需要董事会参与并作出决策的事项已大幅增加。

column1: Furthermore, the amount of reading and preparation required for each meeting is increasing.
column2: 而且，每次会议所需的阅读量和准备工作也在不断增加。

column1: Agendas can become overloaded and this can mean the time for constructive debate must necessarily be restricted in favour of getting through the business.
column2: 议程可能排得过满，为了办完各项事务，留给建设性讨论的时间就势必要受到挤压。
column7: getting through the business|办完各项事务

column1: Often, board business is devolved to committees in order to cope with the workload, which may be more efficient but can mean that the board as a whole is less involved in fully addressing some of the most important issues.
column2: 为应付工作量，董事会事务经常被下放给各个委员会。这样做也许更有效率，却也可能让董事会整体较少参与对某些最重要问题的充分处理。

column1: It is not uncommon for the audit committee meeting to last longer than the main board meeting itself.
column2: 审计委员会的会议比董事会全体会议开得还久，这并不罕见。
column6: main board meeting|董事会全体会议

column1: Process may take the place of discussion and be at the expense of real collaboration, so that boxes are ticked rather than issues tackled.
column2: 程序可能取代讨论，真正的合作也会受到损害。结果，人们只是给清单上的事项逐项打勾，实际问题却没得到处理。
column4: at the expense of|以损害……为代价
column6: boxes are ticked|按清单走完形式

column1: A radical solution, which may work for some very large companies whose businesses are extensive and complex, is the professional board, whose members would work up to three or four days a week, supported by their own dedicated staff and advisers.
column2: 对于某些业务广泛而复杂的大公司，一项可能奏效的彻底改革是设立职业化董事会。成员每周工作时间可多达三四天，并配有专门为他们服务的工作人员和顾问。
column4: extensive and complex|广泛而复杂的

column1: There are obvious risks to this and it would be important to establish clear guidelines for such a board to ensure that it did not step on the toes of management by becoming too engaged in the day-to-day running of the company.
column2: 这种做法显然有风险，因此必须为这样的董事会订立清晰的准则，以免董事会过多介入公司的日常经营，侵占管理层的职权。
column4: establish clear guidelines|确立明确准则
column5: step on the toes of|侵犯……的职权

column1: Problems of recruitment, remuneration and independence could also arise and this structure would not be appropriate for all companies.
column2: 招募董事、确定薪酬和保持独立性也可能遭遇困难，这种组织形式不一定适合所有公司。

column1: However, more professional and better-informed boards would have been particularly appropriate for banks where the executives had access to information that part-time non-executive directors lacked, leaving the latter unable to comprehend or anticipate the 2008 crash.
column2: 然而，对当时的银行来说，更职业化、更了解情况的董事会本来尤其合适。高管能够获得兼职非执行董事所缺乏的信息，以至于后者无法理解或预见2008年的金融崩盘。
column7: part-time non-executive directors|兼职非执行董事

column1: One of the main criticisms of boards and their directors is that they do not focus sufficiently on longer-term matters of strategy, sustainability and governance, but instead concentrate too much on short-term financial metrics.
column2: 对董事会及其成员的一项主要批评，是他们没有充分关注战略、可持续性和公司治理这些长远问题，却把过多的注意力放在短期财务指标上。
column9: short-term financial metrics|短期财务指标

column1: Regulatory requirements and the structure of the market encourage this behaviour.
column2: 监管要求和市场结构都在助长这种行为。
column4: structure of the market|市场结构

column1: The tyranny of quarterly reporting can distort board decision-making, as directors have to ‘make the numbers’ every four months to meet the insatiable appetite of the market for more data.
column2: 季度报告制度的重压可能扭曲董事会的决策，因为董事们每四个月就得“交出达标的数字”，满足市场对更多数据永无止境的渴求。
column7: make the numbers|交出达标的财务数字

column1: This serves to encourage the trading methodology of a certain kind of investor who moves in and out of a stock without engaging in constructive dialogue with the company about strategy or performance, and is simply seeking a short-term financial gain.
column2: 这就助长了某一类投资者的交易方式：他们买进卖出一只股票，却不与公司就战略或业绩进行建设性对话，一心只求短期财务收益。
column5: moves in and out of a stock|买进卖出一只股票
column8: short-term financial gain|短期财务收益

column1: This effect has been made worse by the changing profile of investors due to the globalisation of capital and the increasing use of automated trading systems.
column2: 资本全球化和自动化交易系统的日益普及，改变了投资者群体的构成，使这种影响更加严重。
column7: automated trading systems|自动化交易系统

column1: Corporate culture adapts and management teams are largely incentivised to meet financial goals.
column2: 企业文化随之调整，管理团队获得的激励，主要是为了促使他们达成财务目标。

column1: Compensation for chief executives has become a combat zone where pitched battles between investors, management and board members are fought, often behind closed doors but increasingly frequently in the full glare of press attention.
column2: 首席执行官的薪酬已经成了投资者、管理层和董事会成员激烈交锋的战场。这些较量常在闭门状态下进行，但也越来越多地暴露在媒体强烈的关注之下。
column8: in the full glare of|在……强烈的关注下

column1: Many would argue that this is in the interest of transparency and good governance as shareholders use their muscle in the area of pay to pressure boards to remove underperforming chief executives.
column2: 许多人会认为，这有助于提升透明度和改善公司治理，因为股东借助在薪酬问题上的影响力，向董事会施压，要求撤换表现不佳的首席执行官。
column7: use their muscle|动用自己的影响力

column1: Their powers to vote down executive remuneration policies increased when binding votes came into force.
column2: 具有约束力的表决制度生效后，股东通过投票否决高管薪酬政策的权力增强了。
column4: executive remuneration policies|高管薪酬政策

column1: The chair of the remuneration committee can be an exposed and lonely role, as Alison Carnwath, chair of Barclays Bank’s remuneration committee, found when she had to resign, having been roundly criticised for trying to defend the enormous bonus to be paid to the chief executive; the irony being that she was widely understood to have spoken out against it in the privacy of the committee.
column2: 薪酬委员会主席可能是个孤立无援、又容易成为众矢之的的职位。巴克莱银行薪酬委员会主席艾莉森·卡恩沃思就有切身体会：她试图为将要发给首席执行官的一笔巨额奖金辩护，遭到猛烈批评，不得不辞职。讽刺的是，大家普遍认为，她曾在委员会的闭门会议中明确反对过这笔奖金。
column4: exposed and lonely|易受攻击且孤立无援的
column9: spoken out against|明确表示反对
column10: in the privacy of the committee|在委员会内部的闭门讨论中

column1: The financial crisis stimulated a debate about the role and purpose of the company and a heightened awareness of corporate ethics.
column2: 金融危机催生了关于公司应起何种作用、为何而存在的讨论，也促使人们更加重视企业伦理。
column4: stimulated a debate|引发了一场讨论

column1: Trust in the corporation has been eroded and academics such as Michael Sandel, in his thoughtful and bestselling book What Money Can’t Buy, are questioning the morality of capitalism and the market economy.
column2: 人们对企业的信任已经削弱。迈克尔·桑德尔等学者就此展开了探讨。在颇有洞见的畅销书《金钱不能买什么》中，桑德尔质疑了资本主义和市场经济的道德性。

column1: Boards of companies in all sectors will need to widen their perspective to encompass these issues and this may involve a realignment of corporate goals.
column2: 各行各业的公司董事会都需要拓宽视野，把这些问题纳入考虑，这可能意味着要重新调整企业目标。

column1: We live in challenging times.
column2: 我们生活在一个充满挑战的时代。
